justification: SELECT: central randomisation, double blind, 17604 participants, central laboratory hsCRP assay, multiple imputation prespecified with sensitivity analyses. D5 some concerns only because the analysis is a secondary one within a trial powered for MACE; the hsCRP substudy was prespecified, which is why this is not high risk. Industry funded (Novo Nordisk) with employees among authors.

Same parent trial and same reasoning as the hsCRP substudy. Liver enzymes measured at a central laboratory. Baseline values within the normal range, which limits interpretability but is not a bias domain. Industry funded.

Parent trial (Frias 2018) was adequately randomised and double blind, and biomarkers were measured by immunoassay at central laboratories, so D1, D2 and D4 are low. D3 some concerns: analysis required non-missing baseline and at least one post-baseline value, and stored sample availability governed inclusion. D5 HIGH: the authors state plainly that sample sizes were based on the parent trial's primary endpoints rather than prespecified biomarker analyses, and that this was a post hoc analysis without a prepublished protocol. Ten biomarkers were measured and reported selectively in the narrative. All authors are Eli Lilly employees and shareholders. Overall HIGH, driven by D5.

Parent phase 2 trial randomised and double blind. D5 HIGH for the same reason as Wilson: explicitly an exploratory post hoc analysis, no correction for multiple comparisons applied by the authors' own statement, sample size based on parent trial endpoints. D3 some concerns given analysis-set definitions. Five of six authors are Boehringer Ingelheim employees. Overall HIGH.

Same analysis and same reasoning as trial 1404-0002. Reported separately because it is a distinct trial with a different population (normoglycaemic obesity, 46 weeks) and a different weight covariate.

Randomised double blind placebo controlled phase 2a. Liver fat by MRI-PDFF is an objective centrally read outcome, so D4 low. D3 some concerns: the MASLD substudy population is a subset and attrition over 48 weeks is not fully characterised in the available report. D5 some concerns: liver fat was a prespecified endpoint of this substudy, which is better than the post hoc analyses above, but the four dose arms share a single placebo arm of n=19 and selective dose-arm emphasis is possible. Eli Lilly funded.

D2 HIGH: open label design, which for a weight-sensitive biomarker in an active comparator trial permits differential co-intervention. The authors themselves note the open label design as a limitation and report differential use of new antihypertensive and lipid lowering medication between arms. D3 some concerns: 174 of 515 exenatide and 128 of 514 glimepiride patients discontinued, differential attrition, and patients failing glycaemic control exited the study, which the authors note may have selected for responders. D5 some concerns: hsCRP was a secondary endpoint among many cardiovascular risk markers. Note this trial is ACTIVE CONTROLLED and is excluded from Q2 class contrasts regardless of its risk of bias. Amylin and Eli Lilly funded.
